label: acroscopic
definition: A positional quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being on the side of an axis or its own stalk that faces the apex of the axis that bears it.
reason: A standard term for fern pinnae, veins and sori with no PATO equivalent. PATO_0001234 distal to is a relation and does not mean 'facing the apex'; the sibling term 'basiscopic' would follow. The use on a stigma is odd and should be checked when annotated.

label: coralloid
definition: A branched quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being repeatedly divided into short, thick, blunt and crowded branches, like coral.
reason: A real botanical form (the coralloid roots of cycads, the rhizome of Corallorhiza) that plain 'branched' does not capture. No PATO or FLOPO term exists.
A crest-like callus, lip disc or wing is a raised ridge, which is covered by FLOPO:0991196 crested.

label: hemidimorphic
definition: A dimorphic quality inhering in the set of fronds of a fern by virtue of the fertile fronds differing only partly from the sterile ones, usually being taller, more erect or with narrower fertile pinnae while otherwise similar.
reason: A standard fern term for the step between monomorphic and dimorphic fronds. Mapping it to plain 'dimorphic' would overstate the difference.
'Half-obovoid': an obovoid body flattened on one side. Only one flora uses it, so mapping to the broader obovoid is safer than a new term.
A nail-shaped prickle or outgrowth is a shaft ending in an abruptly widened head. Head-shaped (FLOPO:0991097) is the nearest term, though a nail head is flat rather than rounded.
It means an appendage is absent, but there is no PO or FLOPO class for 'appendage' (anther connective or keel appendage) to state absence of. It stays unannotated until such a class exists.
